title: Size match for container walk: compare per-dimension, not area
trigger: Walking up the DOM to find the farthest same-size container — an ancestor with the same height but a different width (or vice versa) is wrongly accepted because area-based comparison hides the dimensional mismatch
principle: When the contract is 'same height AND width', compare each dimension independently (Math.round(w)===vw && Math.round(h)===vh). Area-based tolerance (|area-ref|/ref <= t) and area-ratio bounds ([0.5,1.5]) accept containers that match one axis but diverge on the other — a wider controls shell with the same height as the video has an area ratio still inside the band, so it gets picked as the player shell and Split View/Player Mode moves the wrong element.

cases.context: themoviebox: video 1226×690, .player-container 1635×690 (same height, +33% width). Area ratio 1.33 is inside the [0.5,1.5] control-shell band, so the isControlShell branch accepts it as the player shell — Split View moves the wider container and the video stage layout breaks.

iframePlayerModeBridge.ts already used per-dimension exact match for the iframe variant — the video variant diverged to area-based tolerance, creating an inconsistency where the same algorithm gave different answers depending on whether the player was an iframe or a same-origin <video>.
cases.good:
// mirror the iframe variant: per-dimension exact match, single shared rule
if (Math.round(r.width) === iw && Math.round(r.height) === ih) farthest = el;

applyFor: Player container / player-shell discovery walking up from a <video> or <iframe>
Fullscreen target selection where the target must visually match the media element on both axes
Any 'find the farthest same-size ancestor' walk where 'same size' means both dimensions, not the product
Split View / Player Mode container resolution on sites with a wider controls shell beside the video
